  If this is your first time, check out https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests-prs
  for our PR guidelines.
-->

## Problem

`vim.text.indent()` had a TODO to support a custom indentation character.

## Solution

Implement the TODO by adding an `opts.prefix` option to `vim.text.indent()`.

comment_data.body:
> For reference, the initial implementation I proposed was meant to follow https://docs.python.org/3/library/textwrap.html#textwrap.indent

I see, though `vim.text.indent()` is a bit different because it has semantics of _setting_ indentation and detecting old one. Python's `indent()` is closer to this

```lua
--- @param text string
--- @param prefix string
--- @return string
function M.prefix(text, prefix)
  return text:gsub('([^\n]*)(\n?)', function(line, nl)
    if line == '' and nl == '' then
      return ''
    end
    if line:match('^%s*$') then
      return line .. nl
    end
    return prefix .. line .. nl
  end)
end
```

Maybe it's too trivial to keep as a separate function, but if anything, it makes more sense to me than exposing it as an option for `vim.text.indent()`.

anyway, with `predicate`, i guess the functionality in this PR will become more useful. @MariaSolOs is this something you had a personal use-case for ?

comment_regular_data.body: I don't think this is news-worthy but lmk if you disagree @justinmk
hmm, this is simpler than i expected. i suppose we can try it, thanks!

> Are you okay with the current implementation though?

would feel more confident if we had a clear use-case. analysis:

### Pros / cons of `opts.prefix`

Pros
- Encapsulates a tricky bit: prefixing *blank* interior lines while *not* emitting a stray prefix after the final `\n`.
- Matches a real, familiar API surface (Python `textwrap.indent`), and composes indent+decorate in one call.

Cons
- It bakes in one blank-line policy (opposite of Python's).
- Second full pass. When `prefix` is set the text is walked twice (indent gsub, then prefix gsub) with a per-line closure.
  - but this is fixable: the whole second gsub exists solely to cover blank lines. to do it in one pass, fold prefixing into the existing `replace_line` (which already runs over `[^\n]+`):
    ```lua
    local function replace_line(line)
      ...
      return line_prefix .. new_indent .. line_text   -- prefix here
    end
    ```
  - also: the early-return optimization now correctly falls through when `line_prefix ~= ''`

Use-cases:
- Email/Markdown blockquote: `{ prefix = '> ' }`
- Comment out a block: `{ prefix = '// ' }`, `{ prefix = '# ' }`
- Diff/log gutters: `{ prefix = '+ ' }`, `{ prefix = '| ' }`



### Alternative: `opts.prefix` decides the "indent char"?

There is currently no way to to force `<tab>` (or an arbitrary char) as the indent char. I'm 90% sure the TODO was for this purpose.

Use-cases:
- Force tabs: convert space-indented text to tabs (or vice-versa) — the natural inverse of `expandtab`, which today is a one-way street (tabs→spaces only).
- Deterministic output: today the indent char is inferred from the *input*, caller can't say "always indent with tabs" without post-processing.
- Visual-guide indent: fill with `·`/`▸` for docs or previews.
@justinmk sounds good, let me re-implement this with your alternative proposal :)

if it only forces the *output*, that again seems like something that is already trivial with a `gsub()` (correct me if wrong)?

sorry, I don't have time to carefully think through this. if we aren't sure what to do here, then let's not rush it. it's fine if the TODO stays a TODO until someone has time to think through the details...
